header.text: Each house of Congress has important leaders, many of whom are determined by which party is in the majority. Look at the chart explaining the functions of some of those leaders. Then answer the question below.

alternativeText.text: A chart showing some of the different roles in Congress and their main functions.   In the House of Representatives, the Speaker of the House is considered the head of the House. They select many committee members and decide which committee will review each bill.  The majority leader serves as the spokesperson for their party, schedules bills, and keeps their party's legislative agenda. The majority whip serves as an assistant to the majority leader, and is responsible for counting the potential votes of representatives.  In the Senate, the vice president of the United States serves as the president of the Senate. They are responsible for breaking tie votes. The president pro tempore serves as the head of the Senate when the president of the Senate is absent. The majority leader serves as a spokesperson for the majority party, but also for the Senate as a whole. They schedule bills and keep the legislative agenda for their party. The majority whip serves as an assistant to the majority leader, and is responsible for counting the potential votes of senators.

header.text: Each house of Congress has important leaders, many of whom are determined by which party is in the majority. Look at the chart explaining the functions of some of those leaders. Then answer the question below.

alternativeText.text: A chart showing some of the different roles in Congress and their main functions.   In the House of Representatives, the Speaker of the House is considered the head of the House. They select many committee members and decide which committee will review each bill.  The majority leader serves as the spokesperson for their party, schedules bills, and keeps their party's legislative agenda. The majority whip serves as an assistant to the majority leader, and is responsible for counting the potential votes of representatives.  In the Senate, the vice president of the United States serves as the president of the Senate. They are responsible for breaking tie votes. The president pro tempore serves as the head of the Senate when the president of the Senate is absent. The majority leader serves as a spokesperson for the majority party, but also for the Senate as a whole. They schedule bills and keep the legislative agenda for their party. The majority whip serves as an assistant to the majority leader, and is responsible for counting the potential votes of senators.

A case starts in the U.S. district courts, which hears all federal court cases and has 94 courts across the country. If the case is appealed, it moves to the U.S. court of appeals, which takes cases appealed from district courts, has 12 regional courts, and decides whether the previous trial was fair. contents.text: The United States Constitution limits what the president can do. If an action is not allowed by the Constitution, the action is called unconstitutional.

Only the federal courts have the power to rule that a president's action is unconstitutional. This power is also known as judicial review. In judicial review, the final decision is up to the Supreme Court of the United States. If the Supreme Court rules that the president's action is unconstitutional, the president is ordered to stop.

Federal courts cannot force the president to follow their orders. Some presidents have even ignored orders from the Supreme Court. However, Congress can impeach a president for not listening to the Supreme Court. Impeaching the president is similar to charging him or her with a crime.

of government in the United States. Read about the levels in the following table. Then answer the question below.

table.text: Federal
The federal government is the national government of the United States. It has the power to make laws that affect the entire country.
State
Within the United States, there are 50 different state governments. State governments have the power to make many decisions that affect only their state.
Local
Within each state, there are many cities, towns, and counties. Each one has a local government to meet the needs of the local community.

contents.text: What makes a punishment "cruel or unusual"? The answer is not clear. The Eighth Amendment doesn't talk about specific punishments. Over time, Americans have changed their views on what is cruel and unusual. For example, the government decided in 2005 that it was cruel to put someone to death for a crime he or she committed before the age of 18.
Today, Americans continue to question what is cruel and unusual. In the future, some punishments used today may be outlawed.
